transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

I’m here because I can’t seem to sit still when I’m supposed to, like in the radiology suite or in class. I feel like I’m crawling out of my skin. I try to tough it out, but I end up shifting around, pacing, or finding some reason to get up and move.
Did this restless feeling start around the time you began or changed any medications?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed it lining up with starting or changing any medication.
Does this urge to move become noticeably worse in the evening or at night?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed it being specifically worse at night.
Did you have similar difficulties with restlessness or sitting still when you were a child?

Yeah, definitely. My parents still bring up those elementary school conferences—teachers would say I was always getting out of my seat, blurting things out, or starting before they’d finished giving directions. It was going on way before middle school, not just recently with radiology training.

latest_inference.note: Childhood onset of pervasive hyperactivity and impulsivity (getting out of seat, blurting out answers) confirms Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, combined presentation, ruling out medication-induced akathisia and generalized anxiety disorder.

inference_history.note: Initial differential for subjective inner restlessness and motor agitation includes drug-induced akathisia, ADHD, restless legs syndrome, and generalized anxiety disorder.
G25.81 is less likely and removed due to the absence of characteristic evening or nocturnal worsening.
